flags.reason: Total enrolled was 30 (15 sham, 15 active); n_subjects reflects only the 15 participants who received active (real) tFUS, per the definition of 'subjects exposed to ultrasound'.
The paper describes a single scanning visit with pre/post tFUS measurements but never explicitly states the number of sessions per participant.

readout_other: Skin conductance response (SCR); self-reported anxiety ratings (0-100 scale) during fear task; resting-state functional connectivity (CONN toolbox) with a left amygdala seed.
direction_notes: Active tFUS decreased amygdala, hippocampal, and dorsal anterior cingulate cortex BOLD activation during a fear task relative to sham; decreased amygdala-insula and amygdala-hippocampal resting-state connectivity and increased amygdala-vmPFC connectivity; the decrease in amygdala activation correlated with decreased self-reported anxiety (r=0.62).
safety_notes: No adverse effects were associated with active tFUS; two participants reported non-unpleasant vibration/tapping sensations at the transducer site during sonication that resolved after sonication ended.

timing.protocol_description: In the MRI scanner, the active tFUS group received 20 min total of 30-s on and 30-s off blocks of sonication to the left amygdala; a specific amygdala sub-nucleus was not targeted.
